# CONTEXT-MAP.md — {PROJECT_NAME}

> **Output file location:** `docs/dev-docs/CONTEXT-MAP.md`.
> **Purpose:** reading router. This project has 100+ documentation files; an agent that
> "reads planning docs" to completion will exhaust its context window before touching code.
> This file answers one question: **for this type of task, open which files — and stop.**

**Rule for agents:** read Tier 0 + the row matching your task type. Do not read
documents beyond that unless something explicitly references them. More context
does not mean better results — irrelevant context pushes relevant context out of the window.

---

## Tier 0 — always read, every task

```
AGENTS.md          ← router: rules of engagement + points to rows below
ARCHITECTURE.md    ← module boundaries, dependency rules, binding decisions
CONVENTIONS.md     ← naming, folder structure, error format, commit format
VERIFY.md          ← gates that must pass before moving columns
OWNERSHIP.md       ← which paths you may write
```

Target total: **< 15 KB**. If it exceeds that, something needs to move to Tier 2.

---

## Routing per task type

| Task type | Additional reading | Do not read |
|---|---|---|
| **New UI page/component** | `contracts/tokens.json`, `docs/design/UI-REFERENCE.md`, `docs/design/SYSTEM.md`, `acceptance/{story}.feature` | backend docs, database, pm |
| **New API endpoint** | `contracts/openapi.yaml`, `contracts/errors.catalog.json`, `docs/architecture/API-REFERENCE.md`, `acceptance/{story}.feature` | design, pm |
| **DB schema change** | `contracts/schema.sql`, `docs/database/ERD.md`, `docs/database/MIGRATIONS.md`, `docs/database/INDEXES.md` | design, frontend |
| **Third-party integration** | `docs/misc/INTEGRATIONS.md`, `docs/deployment/ENVIRONMENTS.md`, `docs/security/REQUIREMENTS.md` | design, pm |
| **Writing tests** | `acceptance/{story}.feature`, `docs/testing/STRATEGY.md`, `contracts/openapi.yaml` | pm, design |
| **Bug fix** | `docs/dev-docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`, `CURRENT-STATE.md`, related module files only | all of docs/planning |
| **Code review** | PR diff, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `references/frontend/anti-slop-core.md`, `docs/security/CHECKLIST.md` | pm, design |
| **Feature touching auth/payments/personal data** | + `docs/security/CHECKLIST.md`, `THREAT-MODEL.md`, `docs/security/COMPLIANCE.md` | — |
| **Refactor** | `ARCHITECTURE.md §3`, related ADRs, `TECHNICAL-DEBT.md` | pm, design |
| **Deploy / release** | `docs/deployment/CHECKLIST.md`, `CI-CD.md`, `ENVIRONMENTS.md`, `docs/operations/INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md` | planning, design |
| **Grooming / task breakdown** | `docs/planning/FSD.md` (relevant section only), `TRACEABILITY-MATRIX.md`, `SCOPE-STATEMENT.md` | architecture detail |

---

## Documents that coding agents NEVER read

These are documents for humans and stakeholders. Coding agents do not need them, and reading
them dilutes context:

```
docs/pm/BUSINESS-CASE.md, PROJECT-CHARTER.md, LEGAL-REGISTER.md, KICKOFF-AGENDA.md,
STAKEHOLDERS.md, COMMUNICATION-PLAN.md, STATUS-REPORTS.md, RETROSPECTIVE.md
docs/planning/ROADMAP.md
docs/pm/BUSINESS-CASE.md
```

Exception: PM/orchestrator agent when preparing sprint reports.

---

## Reading order for project onboarding (once at the start, not per task)

For a new agent or new developer — once only, then rely on routing above:

1. `ARCHITECTURE.md` — shape of the system
2. `docs/dev-docs/MENTAL-MODEL.md` — how the system "thinks"
3. `docs/architecture/FOLDER-STRUCTURE.md` — where things are placed
4. `docs/dev-docs/CURRENT-STATE.md` — how far along we are
5. `CONVENTIONS.md` + `VERIFY.md` — rules of engagement
6. `docs/dev-docs/RUNBOOK-LOCAL.md` — how to run it

Stop there. Open the rest when needed.

---

## When a referenced document does not exist

**Do not fabricate its contents.** Report to the orchestrator: "task X needs `{file}`, file does not exist."
Guessing the contents of a missing document is the most common way an agent produces code that
looks correct and fails silently.
